text:
ryan: Heads up from today's mobile + CLI onboarding test: different sampleapps use REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_CRED, and some mobile examples pull from ~/.redwood/token created by `redwood login`. New hires get stuck.

nadia: Yikes. We've let three convensions live and that's confusing. Proposal: pick REDWOOD_API_KEY as canonical env var, and require explicit REDWOOD_ORG / REDWOOD_PROJECT envs for scoping instead of embedding scope in the key.

pav: Agreed. Also suggest token prefixes to make intent explicit: lk_ for long-lived keys, st_ for short-lived session tokens, mb_ for mobile ephemeral tokens. Put the mapping in docs so teams can programmatically detect runtime.

emily: Parity issue: mobile SDKs currently read ~/.redwood/token; server SDKs read REDWOOD_API_KEY. We should standardize lookup order: CLI flag > REDWOOD_API_KEY > legacy vars (REDWOOD_CRED, REDWOOD_TOKEN) > ~/.redwood/token (only as last resort). SDKs must emit a one-time warning when a legacy source is used.

ryan: Also important: retry behavior. SDKs must not retry on 401. Surface a clear AuthFailure with code "maybe_rotated" and a human hint like "refresh credentials or run 'redwood login'". JS currently retries 401 once due to shared retry logic and that masks rotation problems.

nadia: Telemetry: emit a single event auth.suspected_rotation.per_process when a 401 with Authorization header occurs. No PII; include only token prefix (lk_/st_/mb_) and SDK name+version so ops can detect widespread rotation breaks.

pav: For CI, explicit flow: exchange long-lived lk_ for a short-lived st_. Example script we should add to sampleapps/scripts/ci-exchange.sh: 

# CI exchange
# usage: CI_SECRET contains lk_...
# outputs file .session_token with st_...
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/sessions -H "Authorization: lk_XXX" | jq -r .token > .session_token
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat .session_token)

Let's add the file to sampleapps and include a docker-run example.

emily: Also add cred-lint rule to CI that scans sampleapps/docker-compose.yml, Dockerfiles, and K8s manifests for deprecated env names (REDWOOD_CRED, REDWOOD_TOKEN) and rejects PRs after a 30-day deprecation window. For the next 30 days it should warn only.

ryan: Mobile nuance: prefer in-memory ephemeral tokens for SDKs; if using files, mobile SDK should store tokens in platform secure storage (Keychain/Keystore) not ~/.redwood. Docs should include examples for iOS/Android.

nadia: Parity fixes: I'll take JS + docs (env precedence, token prefixes, retry behavior), pav can do mobile SDKs and sampleapp scripts, emily takes Python + cred-lint integration. I will open a short RFC with timeline + sample scripts + deprecation plan.

bot-deploy: link: https://redwood.internal/devtools/auth-guidelines (autolink)

ryan: Thanks team. Quick checklist to land: 1) docs canonicalizing REDWOOD_API_KEY + REDWOOD_ORG/PROJECT + token prefixes, 2) SDK updates to accept legacy sources but warn once per process, 3) special-case 401 -> AuthFailure no retry + telemetry event, 4) add CI exchange script and Docker example, 5) cred-lint rule in CI with 30/60-day deprecation window. Who can own the RFC?

nadia: I'll draft RFC and include sample scripts and mobile storage guidance.

pav: I'll open PRs for mobile + sampleapp scripts.

emily: I'll do Python SDK patch and hook into cred-lint.

ryan: Great. Let's land docs + sample script before next onboarding cohort.
